metadata.title: Turning Is a Sideways Force, Not a Forward One
metadata.register: formal, undergrad/grad audience, no casual narration
metadata.branding: none — unbranded, book content only, no channel/logo/handle

beats.narration_text: A car rounds a curve at constant speed. What force pulls it toward the center?
beats.new_visual_element: Portrait-only opening question card (title-styled, crimson underline).

beats.narration_text: A car rounds a curve at constant speed. Something must be pulling it off its straight-line path, toward the center of the arc. What force is that?
beats.new_visual_element: Top-down view of a car (dark slate rectangular body, four wheels) on a straight road, a thin black velocity arrow labeled v pointing forward in its direction of travel.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: car on straight road with forward velocity arrow v

beats.narration_text: The road curves into a circular arc. The car's velocity is always tangent to its path, so the arrow rotates smoothly to keep pointing in the current direction of travel, never toward the center.
beats.new_visual_element: The road bends into a circular arc. The car follows it, and the velocity arrow v continuously re-orients to stay tangent to the curve at the car's position.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: car moving along curved road, tangent velocity arrow v updating each instant

beats.narration_text: Freeze the car mid-curve. Notice: nothing in this picture points toward the center of the arc. If no such force exists, Newton's first law says the car keeps going straight, tangent to the curve, and drives off the road.
beats.new_visual_element: The car freezes mid-arc. A dashed circle outline traces the arc's center, with an empty dashed radial line and a crimson question mark hovering where an inward force should be.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: frozen car, dashed arc-center guide, unanswered question mark, velocity arrow v still tangent

beats.narration_text: The missing force is static friction between the tires and the road. It acts sideways, perpendicular to the car's velocity, pointing toward the center of the curve — not forward, and not backward.
beats.new_visual_element: A thick teal arrow grows from the car's tires, perpendicular to v, pointing toward the arc's center, labeled static friction. It replaces the crimson question mark.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: car mid-arc with both v (tangent, black) and centripetal static-friction arrow (teal, inward) visible simultaneously, clearly not parallel

beats.narration_text: As the car completes the curve, that inward friction force stays pinned to the tires, continuously rotating to track the center of the arc, and a glowing trace marks out the circular path behind it.
beats.new_visual_element: The car drives the full arc. A glowing gold trace line follows behind it. The teal inward arrow rotates each instant to keep pointing at the arc's center.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: car has traced most of the arc with a persistent gold trail, teal inward arrow continuously updating

beats.narration_text: Remove that sideways force for even an instant, and the trace snaps straight — the car skids off the road tangent to the curve. Restore it, and the car snaps back onto the arc.
beats.new_visual_element: Mid-arc, the teal arrow briefly vanishes; the gold trace instantly straightens tangent to the curve as the car skids off. A beat later the arrow reappears and the trace snaps back to following the arc.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: gold trail resumes hugging the arc after the brief straight-line skid excursion

beats.narration_text: Turning is not the result of a force pushing you forward. It is the result of a force pulling you in, toward the center of the curve, and that force is static friction.
beats.new_visual_element: Final held frame: completed gold arc trail behind the car, teal inward arrow labeled centripetal force = static friction, small caption beneath reading NOT FORWARD. INWARD.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: final held frame with complete arc, labeled inward arrow, and summary caption
